newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi silent on fate of deported Vietnamese.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi silent on fate of deported Vietnamese.

text.p: Vietnam said investigations into 19 anti-Hanoi activists who were deported to Vietnam from Cambodia earlier this month were continuing, and declined to give details of what had happened to them since their return.
"At present, the Vietnamese offices concerned are carrying out investigations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tran Quang Hoan told reporters at a briefing.
"Of course...in order to arrive at the right conclusions these offices need some time," he added.
Hoan was asked if the Vietnamese activists -- including three women and a monk -- were now being held in prison, but he declined to give details of their whereabouts.

Cambodia deported the 19 activists on December 5, drawing an angry response from the United Nations which said the move violated international rights conventions and could put some of the activists in danger.
Phnom Penh has said the activists were among 28 members of the U.S.-based anti-Hanoi People's Action Party who were detained in Cambodia for allegedly seeking to enter Thailand illegally.
"These 19 people violated Cambodia's law, so they were arrested by the Cambodian government," Hoan said.

"And it was the Cambodian government's initiative to ask Vietnam to receive these people because they are Vietnamese citizens, and according to international practice we accept their return to Vietnam."
